sanskrit: vilāpo bhagnasakthasya yas tu rājño mayā śrutaḥ sa punar hṛdayaṃ kasya krūrasyāpi na nirdahet
english: And that lament of the king whose thighs were shattered, which I heard — whose heart, even the heart of a cruel man, would it not consume with grief?

sanskrit: kasya hy akaruṇasyāpi netrābhyām aśru nāvrajet nṛpater bhagnasakthasya śrutvā tādṛg vacaḥ punaḥ
english: From whose eyes, even a pitiless man's, would tears not flow, on hearing again such words as those of the king whose thighs were broken?

sanskrit: yaś cāyaṃ mitrapakṣo me mayi jīvati nirjitaḥ śokaṃ me vardhayaty eṣa vārivega ivārṇavam ekāgramanaso me 'dya kuto nidrā kutaḥ sukham
english: And the cause of my friends, vanquished while I yet live, swells my sorrow as the rush of waters swells the sea. With my mind fixed on one thing alone this day, whence should sleep come to me, whence any ease?

sanskrit: vāsudevārjunābhyāṃ hi tān ahaṃ parirakṣitān aviṣahyatamān manye mahendreṇāpi mātula
english: Guarded as they are by Vāsudeva and Arjuna, I hold them, uncle, to be utterly unassailable, even by mighty Indra himself.

sanskrit: na cāsmi śakyaḥ saṃyantum asmāt kāryāt kathaṃ cana na taṃ paśyāmi loke 'smin yo māṃ kāryān nivartayet iti me niścitā buddhir eṣā sādhumatā ca me
english: Nor can I in any way be restrained from this deed; I see no one in this world who could turn me back from my purpose. This is my settled resolve, and I deem it right.

sanskrit: vārttikaiḥ kathyamānas tu mitrāṇāṃ me parābhavaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca vijayo hṛdayaṃ dahatīva me
english: The ruin of my friends, told to me by the messengers, and the victory of the Pāṇḍavas — these all but burn my heart away.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu kadanaṃ kṛtvā śatrūṇām adya sauptike tato viśramitā caiva svaptā ca vigatajvaraḥ
english: But once I have wrought slaughter among my foes this night while they sleep, then I shall take my rest, and sleep at last, my fever gone.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca śuśrūṣur api durmedhāḥ puruṣo 'niyatendriyaḥ nālaṃ vedayituṃ kṛtsnau dharmārthāv iti me matiḥ
english: Kṛpa said: A man dull of wit and unrestrained in his senses, though eager to learn, is not able to grasp duty and gain in their fullness — such is my thought.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvan medhāvī vinayaṃ yo na śikṣati na ca kiṃ cana jānāti so 'pi dharmārthaniścayam
english: Likewise the keen-witted man who is not schooled in discipline knows nothing whatever of the sure judgment of duty and gain.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣus tv eva medhāvī puruṣo niyatendriyaḥ jānīyād āgamān sarvān grāhyaṃ ca na virodhayet
english: But the keen-witted man, eager to learn and restrained in his senses, would understand all the sacred teachings and would not contend against what ought to be accepted.

sanskrit: aneyas tv avamānī yo durātmā pāpapūruṣaḥ diṣṭam utsṛjya kalyāṇaṃ karoti bahupāpakam
english: But the ungovernable man, scornful, evil-souled and base, casting aside the blessed path ordained, performs deeds heavy with sin.

sanskrit: nāthavantaṃ tu suhṛdaḥ pratiṣedhanti pātakāt nivartate tu lakṣmīvān nālakṣmīvān nivartate
english: Friends restrain from wrongdoing the man who heeds them; the man of good fortune turns back, but the luckless man turns not back.

sanskrit: yathā hy uccāvacair vākyaiḥ kṣiptacitto niyamyate tathaiva suhṛdā śakyo naśakyas tv avasīdati
english: As a man whose mind is troubled is steadied by words now stern, now gentle, so too the tractable man can be guided by a friend; but the untractable comes to ruin.

sanskrit: tathaiva suhṛdaṃ prājñaṃ kurvāṇaṃ karma pāpakam prājñāḥ saṃpratiṣedhante yathāśakti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Even so, when a wise friend sets about an evil deed, the wise restrain him with all their power, again and again.

sanskrit: sa kalyāṇe matiṃ kṛtvā niyamyātmānam ātmanā kuru me vacanaṃ tāta yena paścān na tapyase
english: Set your mind, then, upon the good, restraining yourself by yourself; heed my word, my son, that you may not grieve hereafter.

sanskrit: na vadhaḥ pūjyate loke suptānām iha dharmataḥ tathaiva nyastaśastrāṇāṃ vimuktarathavājinām
english: The slaying of those who sleep is not honored in this world by the law of righteousness, nor the slaying of those who have laid down their weapons and unyoked their chariots and steeds.

sanskrit: ye ca brūyus tavāsmīti ye ca syuḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ vimuktamūrdhajā ye ca ye cāpi hatavāhanāḥ
english: Nor of those who would say, 'I am yours,' nor of those who have come for refuge, nor of those whose hair has come loose, nor of those whose mounts are slain.

sanskrit: adya svapsyanti pāñcālā vimuktakavacā vibho viśvastā rajanīṃ sarve pretā iva vicetasaḥ
english: This night the Pāñcālas will sleep, lord, their armor cast off, all of them trusting and unwary through the night, like the senseless dead.

sanskrit: yas teṣāṃ tadavasthānāṃ druhyeta puruṣo 'nṛjuḥ vyaktaṃ sa narake majjed agādhe vipule 'plave
english: The crooked man who should do them violence while they are in such a state would surely sink into a hell bottomless, vast, and without a raft to bear him.

sanskrit: sarvāstraviduṣāṃ loke śreṣṭhas tvam asi viśrutaḥ na ca te jātu loke 'smin susūkṣmam api kilbiṣam
english: In all the world you are renowned as the foremost of those skilled in every weapon, and never in this world has even the slightest stain clung to you.

sanskrit: tvaṃ punaḥ sūryasaṃkāśaḥ śvobhūta udite ravau prakāśe sarvabhūtānāṃ vijetā yudhi śātravān
english: You, again, are like the sun: when the dawn comes and the sun has risen, in the sight of all beings you shall conquer your foes in open battle.

sanskrit: asaṃbhāvitarūpaṃ hi tvayi karma vigarhitam śukle raktam iva nyastaṃ bhaved iti matir mama
english: A blameworthy deed would be a thing unthinkable in you — like a stain of red set upon white cloth: such is my thought.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca evam etad yathāttha tvam anuśāsmīha mātula tais tu pūrvamayaṃ setuḥ śatadhā vidalīkṛtaḥ
english: Aśvatthāman said: It is so, even as you instruct me here, uncle. But by them was this dyke of righteousness first shattered into a hundred pieces.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ bhūmipālānāṃ bhavatāṃ cāpi saṃnidhau nyastaśastro mama pitā dhṛṣṭadyumnena pātitaḥ
english: Before the very eyes of the lords of earth, and in your presence too, my father, having laid down his weapon, was struck down by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: karṇaś ca patite cakre rathasya rathināṃ varaḥ uttame vyasane sanno hato gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: And Karṇa, foremost of chariot-warriors, when the wheel of his chariot had sunk down, caught in dire distress, was slain by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: tathā śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo nyastaśastro nirāyudhaḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya hato gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: So too Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, his weapon laid down and unarmed, was slain by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, who set Śikhaṇḍin before him.

sanskrit: bhūriśravā maheṣvāsas tathā prāyagato raṇe krośatāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ yuyudhānena pātitaḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, the great archer, having sat down in the rite of fasting unto death upon the field, was struck down by Yuyudhāna while the lords of earth cried out against it.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca bhīmena sametya gadayā mṛdhe paśyatāṃ bhūmipālānām adharmeṇa nipātitaḥ
english: And Duryodhana, meeting Bhīma with the mace in combat, was felled by foul means in the sight of the lords of earth.

sanskrit: ekākī bahubhis tatra parivārya mahārathaiḥ adharmeṇa naravyāghro bhīmasenena pātitaḥ
english: Alone, hemmed in there by many great chariot-warriors, that tiger among men was felled unrighteously by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: vilāpo bhagnasakthasya yo me rājñaḥ pariśrutaḥ vārttikānāṃ kathayatāṃ sa me marmāṇi kṛntati
english: The lament of my king whose thighs were shattered, which I have heard from the telling of the messengers, cuts me to the quick.

sanskrit: evam adhārmikāḥ pāpāḥ pāñcālā bhinnasetavaḥ tān evaṃ bhinnamaryādān kiṃ bhavān na vigarhati
english: Thus lawless and sinful are the Pāñcālas, breakers of the dyke of right. Why does your honor not condemn them, who have so broken every bound?

sanskrit: pitṛhantṝn ahaṃ hatvā pāñcālān niśi sauptike kāmaṃ kīṭaḥ pataṃgo vā janma prāpya bhavāmi vai
english: Having slain in the night, as they sleep, the Pāñcālas who killed my father, I am content, even if I be reborn as a worm or a moth.

sanskrit: tvare cāham anenādya yad idaṃ me cikīrṣitam tasya me tvaramāṇasya kuto nidrā kutaḥ sukham
english: And I make haste this day toward this that I am resolved to do; for me who hasten so, whence should sleep come, whence any ease?

sanskrit: na sa jātaḥ pumāṃl loke kaś cin na ca bhaviṣyati yo me vyāvartayed etāṃ vadhe teṣāṃ kṛtāṃ matim
english: There is born in this world no man, nor shall there ever be, who could turn me from this resolve I have set upon their slaying.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā mahārāja droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān ekānte yojayitvāśvān prāyād abhimukhaḥ parān
english: Saṃjaya said: Having so spoken, great king, the valiant son of Droṇa yoked his horses apart and set forth straight toward his foes.

sanskrit: tam abrūtāṃ mahātmānau bhojaśāradvatāv ubhau kim ayaṃ syandano yuktaḥ kiṃ ca kāryaṃ cikīrṣitam
english: To him the two great-souled ones, the Bhoja and the son of Śaradvat, said: Why is this chariot yoked, and what deed do you intend to do?

sanskrit: ekasārthaṃ prayātau svas tvayā saha nararṣabha samaduḥkhasukhau caiva nāvāṃ śaṅkitum arhasi
english: We two have set out together with you on one road, O bull among men, sharing alike your grief and joy; you should not mistrust us.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu saṃkruddhaḥ pitur vadham anusmaran tābhyāṃ tathyaṃ tadācakhyau yad asyātmacikīrṣitam
english: Then Aśvatthāman, kindled to wrath as he recalled his father's slaying, told them truly what he was resolved within himself to do.

sanskrit: hatvā śatasahasrāṇi yodhānāṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ nyastaśastro mama pitā dhṛṣṭadyumnena pātitaḥ
english: When he had slain warriors by the hundred thousand with his keen arrows, my father, his weapon laid down, was struck down by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: taṃ tathaiva haniṣyāmi nyastavarmāṇam adya vai putraṃ pāñcālarājasya pāpaṃ pāpena karmaṇā
english: Just so will I slay this very day, with his armor cast off, that sinful son of the Pāñcāla king — by a deed as foul as his own.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca nihataḥ pāpaḥ pāñcālaḥ paśuvan mayā śastrāhavajitāṃ lokān prāpnuyād iti me matiḥ
english: And how should that wicked Pāñcāla, slain by me like a beast, attain the worlds won by the valor of arms in battle? Such is my thought.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ saṃnaddhakavacau sakhaḍgāv āttakārmukau samāsthāya pratīkṣetāṃ rathavaryau paraṃtapau
english: Quickly, then, your armor girt on, swords at your sides and bows in hand, mount your noble chariots, you scorchers of foes, and wait for me.

sanskrit: ity uktvā ratham āsthāya prāyād abhimukhaḥ parān tam anvagāt kṛpo rājan kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ
english: Having spoken thus, he mounted his chariot and set forth straight toward his foes; and Kṛpa, O king, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas followed him.

sanskrit: te prayātā vyarocanta parān abhimukhās trayaḥ hūyamānā yathā yajñe samiddhā havyavāhanāḥ
english: As they went forth, the three of them, facing their foes, shone like three blazing sacrificial fires being fed with oblations at a sacrifice.

sanskrit: yayuś ca śibiraṃ teṣāṃ saṃprasuptajanaṃ vibho dvāradeśaṃ tu saṃprāpya drauṇis tasthau rathottame
english: And they came to the camp of their foes, where the folk lay deep in sleep, lord; and reaching the place of the gate, the son of Droṇa halted upon his splendid chariot.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dvāradeśe tato drauṇim avasthitam avekṣya tau akurvatāṃ bhojakṛpau kiṃ saṃjaya vadasva me
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When they beheld the son of Droṇa halted there at the place of the gate, what did those two, the Bhoja and Kṛpa, do? Tell me, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṛtavarmāṇam āmantrya kṛpaṃ ca sa mahāratham drauṇir manyuparītātmā śibiradvāram āsadat
english: Saṃjaya said: Bidding Kṛtavarman and the great chariot-warrior Kṛpa await him, the son of Droṇa, his soul possessed by fury, drew near the gate of the camp.

sanskrit: tatra bhūtaṃ mahākāyaṃ candrārkasadṛśadyutim so 'paśyad dvāram āvṛtya tiṣṭhantaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: There he beheld a being of vast body, of splendor like the moon and the sun, standing and barring the gate, terrible enough to make the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: vasānaṃ carma vaiyāghraṃ mahārudhiravisravam kṛṣṇājinottarāsaṅgaṃ nāgayajñopavītinam
english: He was clad in a tiger's skin streaming with great gouts of blood, a black antelope-hide for his upper garment, and a serpent for his sacred thread.

sanskrit: bāhubhiḥ svāyataiḥ pīnair nānāpraharaṇodyataiḥ baddhāṅgadamahāsarpaṃ jvālāmālākulānanam
english: With his long, massive arms raised aloft bearing weapons of every kind, great serpents bound about him for armlets, his face wreathed in garlands of flame —

sanskrit: daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaṃ vyāditāsyaṃ bhayāvaham nayanānāṃ sahasraiś ca vicitrair abhibhūṣitam
english: his mouth dreadful with fangs and gaping wide, a thing of terror, adorned with thousands of wondrous eyes of many hues.

sanskrit: naiva tasya vapuḥ śakyaṃ pravaktuṃ veṣa eva vā sarvathā tu tad ālakṣya sphuṭeyur api parvatāḥ
english: Neither his form nor his very garb could be told in words; and at the sight of it, the very mountains might burst asunder.

sanskrit: tasyāsyān nāsikābhyāṃ ca śravaṇābhyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ tebhyaś cākṣisahasrebhyaḥ prādurāsan mahārciṣaḥ
english: From his mouth, from his nostrils, from his ears on every side, and from those thousands of eyes, there blazed forth mighty tongues of flame.

sanskrit: tathā tejomarīcibhyaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharāḥ prādurāsan hṛṣīkeśāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And from those rays of blazing light there appeared, by the hundred and the thousand, forms of Hṛṣīkeśa, each bearing conch and discus and mace.

sanskrit: tad atyadbhutam ālokya bhūtaṃ lokabhayaṃkaram drauṇir avyathito divyair astravarṣair avākirat
english: Beholding that most wondrous being, terror of the worlds, the son of Droṇa, unshaken, overwhelmed it with showers of celestial weapons.

sanskrit: drauṇimuktāñ śarāṃs tāṃs tu tad bhūtaṃ mahad agrasat udadher iva vāryoghān pāvako vaḍavāmukhaḥ
english: But that great being devoured those arrows loosed by the son of Droṇa, as the submarine fire devours the floods of the sea.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu saṃprekṣya tāñ śaraughān nirarthakān rathaśaktiṃ mumocāsmai dīptām agniśikhām iva
english: Aśvatthāman, seeing those floods of arrows spent in vain, hurled at it the spear from his chariot, blazing like a tongue of fire.

sanskrit: sā tadāhatya dīptāgrā rathaśaktir aśīryata yugānte sūryam āhatya maholkeva divaś cyutā
english: That spear with its blazing point struck the being and shattered to pieces, like a great meteor fallen from the sky striking the sun at the world's end.

sanskrit: atha hematsaruṃ divyaṃ khaḍgam ākāśavarcasam kośāt samudbabarhāśu bilād dīptam ivoragam
english: Then he swiftly drew from its sheath a celestial sword with hilt of gold and the sheen of the sky, like a glowing serpent drawn forth from its hole.

sanskrit: tataḥ khaḍgavaraṃ dhīmān bhūtāya prāhiṇot tadā sa tadāsādya bhūtaṃ vai vilayaṃ tūlavad yayau
english: Then the wise one flung that excellent sword at the being; but reaching that being, it dissolved away like a wisp of cotton.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kupito drauṇir indraketunibhāṃ gadām jvalantīṃ prāhiṇot tasmai bhūtaṃ tām api cāgrasat
english: Then the son of Droṇa, enraged, hurled at it a blazing mace like the banner of Indra; but the being devoured that too.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāyudhābhāve vīkṣamāṇas tatas tataḥ apaśyat kṛtam ākāśam anākāśaṃ janārdanaiḥ
english: Then, all his weapons gone, gazing this way and that, he saw the whole sky made no longer sky, filled with forms of Janārdana.

sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ dṛṣṭvā droṇaputro nirāyudhaḥ abravīd abhisaṃtaptaḥ kṛpavākyam anusmaran
english: Beholding that most wondrous sight, the son of Droṇa, now without a weapon, scorched with anguish, recalling the words of Kṛpa, spoke aloud.

sanskrit: bruvatām apriyaṃ pathyaṃ suhṛdāṃ na śṛṇoti yaḥ sa śocaty āpadaṃ prāpya yathāham ativartya tau
english: He who heeds not friends when they speak the wholesome word, though it be unwelcome, grieves when he meets with calamity — as I do now, having disregarded those two.

sanskrit: śāstradṛṣṭān avadhyān yaḥ samatītya jighāṃsati sa pathaḥ pracyuto dharmyāt kupathaṃ pratipadyate
english: He who, passing over those whom scripture holds inviolable, seeks to slay them, falls from the path of righteousness and enters upon an evil road.

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇanṛpastrīṣu sakhyur mātur guros tathā vṛddhabālajaḍāndheṣu suptabhītotthiteṣu ca
english: Against cows, brahmins, kings, and women, against a friend, a mother, a teacher, against the old, the young, the dull-witted and the blind, against the sleeping, the terror-struck, and one just risen —

sanskrit: mattonmattapramatteṣu na śastrāṇy upadhārayet ity evaṃ gurubhiḥ pūrvam upadiṣṭaṃ nṛṇāṃ sadā
english: against the drunken, the mad, and the heedless — one should not draw weapons. So in former times have teachers ever instructed men.

sanskrit: so 'ham utkramya panthānaṃ śāstradṛṣṭaṃ sanātanam amārgeṇaivam ārabhya ghorām āpadam āgataḥ
english: I, having stepped beyond the eternal path that scripture shows, and so set out upon a way that is no way, have come to a dreadful calamity.

sanskrit: tāṃ cāpadaṃ ghoratarāṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ yad udyamya mahat kṛtyaṃ bhayād api nivartate
english: And the wise call that the most dreadful calamity of all, when a man, having set about some great deed, turns back from it through fear.

sanskrit: aśakyaṃ caiva kaḥ kartuṃ śaktaḥ śaktibalād iha na hi daivād garīyo vai mānuṣaṃ karma kathyate
english: And who here is able by the strength of his power to do what cannot be done? For the deed of man is never said to outweigh fate.

sanskrit: mānuṣaṃ kurvataḥ karma yadi daivān na sidhyati sa pathaḥ pracyuto dharmyād vipadaṃ pratipadyate
english: If for the man who does a human deed it succeeds not because of fate, then, fallen from the path of righteousness, he meets with disaster.

sanskrit: pratighātaṃ hy avijñātaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ yad ārabhya kriyāṃ kāṃ cid bhayād iha nivartate
english: The wise call it an unforeseen thwarting when a man, having begun some undertaking, turns back from it here through fear.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ duṣpraṇītena bhayaṃ māṃ samupasthitam na hi droṇasutaḥ saṃkhye nivarteta kathaṃ cana
english: This terror has come upon me through ill-guided conduct; yet the son of Droṇa could in no wise turn back in battle.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca sumahad bhūtaṃ daivadaṇḍam ivodyatam na caitad abhijānāmi cintayann api sarvathā
english: And this exceedingly mighty being, raised up like the rod of fate — this I do not recognize, however I ponder it in every way.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ yeyam adharme me pravṛttā kaluṣā matiḥ tasyāḥ phalam idaṃ ghoraṃ pratighātāya dṛśyate
english: Surely this defiled resolve of mine, bent upon unrighteousness — this dreadful fruit of it is seen here, set to thwart me.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ daivavihitaṃ mama saṃkhye nivartanam nānyatra daivād udyantum iha śakyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: This turning-back of mine in battle is ordained by fate; and save by fate there is no power here in any way to act.

sanskrit: so 'ham adya mahādevaṃ prapadye śaraṇaṃ prabhum daivadaṇḍam imaṃ ghoraṃ sa hi me nāśayiṣyati
english: Therefore this day I take refuge with Mahādeva, the Lord; for he it is who will destroy for me this dreadful rod of fate.

sanskrit: kapardinaṃ prapadyātha devadevam umāpatim kapālamālinaṃ rudraṃ bhaganetraharaṃ haram
english: I take refuge with the matted-haired one, god of gods, lord of Umā, with Rudra wreathed in skulls, Hara, who tore out the eye of Bhaga.

sanskrit: sa hi devo 'tyagād devāṃs tapasā vikrameṇa ca tasmāc charaṇam abhyeṣye giriśaṃ śūlapāṇinam
english: For that god surpassed all the gods by his austerity and his valor; therefore will I go for refuge to the dweller on the mountain, the bearer of the trident.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa evaṃ cintayitvā tu droṇaputro viśāṃ pate avatīrya rathopasthād dadhyau saṃprayataḥ sthitaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having thought thus, the son of Droṇa, O lord of peoples, descended from the floor of his chariot and, standing in earnest devotion, fell to meditating.
